Escalated to `effort:max`. I release the claim. No branch was pushed and no code is held.

## What I found

I reproduced the failure on upstream/main `a7afb5766`. The two tests give the same nine `RapidInPart` warnings.

Each flagged move is a vertical rapid straight up from the end of a raster feed, under the lying swarf pose (axis `[1,0,0]` or `[-1,0,0]`). This is the swarf exit rise of #48 (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp_rise.rs`, `rapid_rise`).

The verifier is correct. I measured each lift with the solid law of the verifier (`judged` in `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs`, cutting edge only, allowance found by bisection):

| Move | Start pose at allow 0.01 | Depth of the lift in the part |
|---|---|---|
| 2141 | clean | 0.013 mm |
| 2265 | clean | 0.240 mm |
| 2391, 2517, 2643 | clean | 0.093 mm |
| 2743, 2868, 2989, 3110 | clean | 0.082 mm |

The start pose of each lift is clean. So the contact left by the cut does not cause the warning, and the #4211 lift-out-of-the-kerf rule does not apply. The lift itself goes into the part. A looser verifier law is therefore the wrong fix.

Likely cause: #4108 (`010ec695d`, #4062) added the vertical-rapid sweep for Envelope paths. Before that change, nothing judged these rises, so they passed silently.

## Why `rapid_rise` accepts these lifts

- `flank_clear` permits the flank to stand at `r - tol` (0.1 mm into the contact band). That is the cut allowance, not the rapid allowance. The verifier gives a rapid only the tightened gouge tolerance (0.01 on this blade).
- The proof samples the rise every `r/2` (1.5 mm) up Z. It also samples the flank every `r/2` along the axis. With r = 3, a facet vertex between samples is not seen. Spheres at `r/2` spacing cover a cylinder only to about `0.968 r`, which is 0.1 mm short.
- Move 2141 starts below the equator of the tube (z = -0.24). A pure Z lift from there moves toward the facet vertex at z = 0. The proof has no test for the direction of the contact normal.

## What a fix needs

The rise proof in `rapid_rise` must become exact or conservative for the rapid law:

1. The ball and the flank must clear the part by the rapid allowance, not by `r - tol`.
2. The proof must account for the gap between its samples, or use an exact distance from the swept strip to each facet.
3. A rise must not start toward a contact whose normal points down.

A rise that the proof does not accept keeps the upright feed and the air link, as before #48. This changes the swarf programs (link counts and posted G-code), and it can move swarf goldens and catalog programs. It is a new clearance proof in the generator, which is a collision law. So I raise the effort to `max`.

## What I tried and dropped

I tried a verifier rule that grants a leaning lift the depth of its start pose. All nine start poses were clean, so the rule had no effect. The lifts are real penetrations, so I removed the rule.
